name: PAD Open Lower Extremity Revascularization with Acute Kidney Injury
remarks: Models the full clinical pathway for peripheral arterial disease (PAD) from initial
diagnosis through treatment strategy selection, and — for patients who receive open
lower extremity revascularization (OLER) — through a 7-day post-operative acute
kidney injury (AKI) outcome window.
Clinical workflow:
1a. PAD onset delay: Uniform(0, 20) years after age 60 (onset age 60-80)
1b. PAD diagnosis (ConditionOnset) — capped at age 90
2. Outpatient PAD diagnosis encounter
3. Document presenting symptom (asymptomatic, claudication, rest pain, wound/tissue loss)
4. Document comorbidities (smoking, diabetes, hypertension, COPD, CHF, baseline chronic
kidney disease/ESRD, functional impairment) and anthropometrics (BMI, height, weight)
5. Ankle-brachial index (ABI) measurement
6. End outpatient encounter
7. Treatment strategy decision:
- Medical management (10%) → Terminal
- Endovascular revascularization (10%) → Terminal
- Open surgical revascularization (80%) → AKI pathway
8. Pre-surgical workup delay (1-6 months)
9. Historical prior revascularization (25%)
10. Pre-index non-prophylaxis antibiotic (20%, admission-time, unrelated infection)
11. Urgency flag (25% urgent/emergent)
12. Inpatient surgical admission → perioperative cefazolin → open revascularization
13. Post-operative AKI risk check (0-7 days post-procedure, KDIGO-aligned window)
14. Post-operative inpatient stay (3-7 days) → discharge (disposition varies by AKI stage)
Cohort definitions:
Target  : inpatient surgery for open lower extremity revascularization (OLER)
Outcome : AKI diagnosis within 0-7 days of index surgery (matches
pad-oler-aki-desc/inst/sql/sql_server/*.sql window:
'A.START_DATE >= DATEADD(day,0,P.START_DATE) AND
A.START_DATE <= DATEADD(day,7,P.START_DATE)')
AKI incidence and severity assumptions (marginal, fixed — not comorbidity-adjusted,
same simplification used by pad_ssi.json's fixed SSI incidence):
Fixed post-op AKI incidence: 18% (consistent with reported 15-20% incidence after
open vascular/lower-extremity revascularization surgery)
AKI stage distribution (of all AKI cases, KDIGO-aligned):
Stage 1 (mild)             : 60% (10.8% of all patients) — resolves inpatient, no RRT
Stage 2 (moderate)         : 25% ( 4.5% of all patients) — resolves inpatient, no RRT
Stage 3 (severe, dialysis) : 15% ( 2.7% of all patients) — requires renal dialysis (RRT)
Baseline comorbidity prevalence assumptions in this surgical PAD population:
Current smoker                       : 35%
Type 2 diabetes mellitus             : 30%
Obesity (BMI >= 30)                  : 40%
Hypertension                         : 60%
COPD                                 : 20%
CHF                                  : 15%
Baseline chronic kidney disease (CKD): 20% — major AKI risk factor and the same
population the 7 reused surg-aki-desc outcome cohorts must correctly EXCLUDE from
'incident AKI' via their -365..-1 day (and <= index date) baseline lookback windows.
Of baseline-CKD patients, 20% (4% overall) are already end-stage renal disease (ESRD)
on chronic dialysis at baseline — deliberately included so the outcome SQL's ESRD/
dialysis exclusion logic has real prevalent cases to exclude, not just an empty check.
Functional status (Barthel survey):
Independent transfers and ambulation : 75%
Ambulation with 1-person help        : 15%
Wheelchair bound                     : 10%
Presenting symptom distribution (Rutherford-aligned):
Asymptomatic (Rutherford 0)          : 10%
Claudication (Rutherford 1-3)        : 50%
Rest pain (Rutherford 4)             : 25%
Wound / tissue loss (Rutherford 5-6) : 15%
Treatment strategy distribution (oversampled for open surgical to maximize AKI outcome
data, same oversampling rationale as pad_ssi.json):
Medical management only              : 10%
Endovascular revascularization       : 10%
Open surgical revascularization      : 80%

Timing:
Pre-surgical workup delay : 1-6 months after PAD diagnosis
Inpatient stay            : 3-7 days post-surgery
AKI onset window          : 0-7 days post-procedure (KDIGO-aligned; matches the
outcome SQL's DATEADD(day,0..7,P.START_DATE) window)
Stage 1/2 AKI resolution  : 2-5 days after onset, before or at discharge
Stage 3 (dialysis) onset  : persists through discharge — RRT dependence not modeled
as resolving (out of scope; see 'Does NOT model' below)
Usage:
Copy to <synthea_home>/src/main/resources/modules/ and run Synthea normally.
To load into an omop_synth database, run this project's Step 5 CSV-to-OMOP ETL
workflow against the generated CSV output.
Does NOT model: mortality, limb loss, graft failure, recurrent PAD, kidney transplant
recipients, or eventual renal recovery for stage 3 (dialysis-dependent) AKI.
PAD onset delay: Uniform(0, 20) years after age 60 (onset age 60-80).
Mirrors pad_ssi.json's PAD_Onset_Delay so the underlying PAD population
is generated the same way — only the post-procedure outcome differs.
Cap the PAD pathway at age 90. Patients older than 90 after the
onset delay are routed to Terminal so procedure ages stay realistic.

Current smoking prevalence in PAD patients is modeled at 35%.
Type 2 diabetes prevalence in PAD patients is modeled at 30%.
Baseline chronic kidney disease (CKD) prevalence in this surgical PAD population
is modeled at 20% — a major, well-documented risk factor for post-operative AKI.
Of baseline-CKD patients, 20% (4% overall) have progressed to end-stage renal
disease (ESRD) already on chronic dialysis; the remaining 80% (16% overall) have
non-dialysis-dependent CKD. This split gives the reused surg-aki-desc outcome
cohorts' ESRD/dialysis baseline exclusion logic real prevalent cases to filter out.

codes.display: Fluoroscopy guided percutaneous transluminal angioplasty of peripheral artery with contrast

remarks: Endovascular revascularization (balloon angioplasty or stenting).
Not an open surgery — does not enter the AKI outcome pathway.
Urgency is determined immediately after the treatment strategy decision.
25% of open surgical procedures are flagged urgent or emergent — urgent/emergent
surgery is itself an AKI risk factor (contrast exposure, hypotension), though not
separately modeled as raising the fixed marginal AKI rate in this version.
Using type Procedure (not Observation) routes the record to synthea.procedures,
which the ETL maps into OMOP procedure_occurrence via SNOMED-CT 73994005 →
standard concept 4158569 (Emergency procedure, Procedure domain).
Time from PAD evaluation to open revascularization surgery.
Includes pre-operative imaging, cardiac/renal risk stratification, and scheduling.
Range: 1-6 months.
20% of admitted patients start a non-prophylactic cephalexin course at the time of
admission (e.g. pre-operative treatment of a concurrent skin/soft-tissue infection).
The course runs 3-7 days and precedes the perioperative cefazolin prophylaxis.
The remaining 80% proceed directly to the pre-operative delay and then cefazolin.
Treatment-length antibiotic course started at admission: 3-7 days.
Pre-operative optimisation window between admission and surgery: 0-7 days.
All admission paths (with or without cephalexin) merge here before the
perioperative prophylactic antibiotic and revascularisation procedure.
Single-dose perioperative cefazolin per SCIP/ACS NSQIP guidelines.
Ended immediately after the procedure.

Marginal post-op AKI incidence held fixed at 18%, split across KDIGO stages:
10.8% -> Stage 1 (mild, resolves, no dialysis)
4.5% -> Stage 2 (moderate, resolves, no dialysis)
2.7% -> Stage 3 (severe, dialysis-requiring)
All AKI onset timing is anchored to this state (immediately post-procedure,
antibiotic prophylaxis just ended) so the 0-7 day post-op Delay below stays
within the outcome SQL's DATEADD(day,0..7,P.START_DATE) window regardless of
how long the inpatient stay itself runs.
Time from procedure to Stage 1 AKI diagnosis: post-op day 1-4 (within the
0-7 day outcome window and typically caught on routine post-op labs).

All AKI branches (including no-AKI) merge here before discharge disposition.
Discharge disposition tracks the joint (AKI stage, will-develop-dialysis-
dependence) outcome computed in AKI_Risk_Branch. This state cannot itself see
which AKI branch was taken, so disposition is approximated as three population-
level weighted groups matching the AKI_Risk_Branch proportions:
82.0% no AKI              -> 20% rehab / 80% home
15.3% stage 1/2 (resolved)-> 30% rehab / 70% home
2.7% stage 3 (dialysis)  -> 60% rehab-or-SNF / 40% home with outpatient dialysis
